chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I prayed behind Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) at midday, and I said, 'By my father and my mother, what is the time for Asr?' He said, 'The time when you kneel your camels.' I said, 'When it is not during a journey?' He said, 'When the shadow is less than one foot, less than two-thirds of a foot, it is the time for Asr.'

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Midday, when the sun reaches its zenith
key_terms.تَسْقِيلُ إِبِلَكَ: Literal: kneeling your camels; a metaphorical time reference for late afternoon

ai.seo_question: What is the precise definition of the time for Asr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise onset of Asr time by using the shadow of a standard object (a foot) as a practical measure, distinguishing it from the later time associated with resting camels (Qailulah). This hadith is central to the Shia jurisprudence of 'Jam' al-Taqdim' (early conjunction), providing the specific temporal boundary that allows for combining Dhuhr and Asr prayers during travel or in cases of necessity, thereby emphasizing the flexibility within the fixed prayer times.
